title: A controlled pilot for Sterling FinTech
summary: Establish a measurable, review-led pilot before making a wider delivery commitment. Turn verified usage metrics into review-ready QBR narratives, with a CSM accountable for every customer-facing draft.
goals: Demonstrate a measurable improvement in the agreed pilot workflow.
Ensure every numerical claim reconciles to a verified metric snapshot.
Prove the value and controls needed for a wider rollout.
inScope: Discovery-led confirmation of one agreed usage-data export and one QBR narrative template.
Drafts with metric references, period labels and missing-data flags.
SSO for pilot users and an approved deployment region.
A pilot with 5 CSMs and up to 10 fictional or approved test accounts.
outOfScope: Autonomous customer delivery or CRM write-back.
Predictive revenue claims or invented benchmarks.
Replacing dashboards, rebuilding the data warehouse or all QBR templates.
Organisation-wide rollout, multilingual output and ongoing managed service.
Additional data sources and workflows beyond the signed-off pilot boundary.

assumptions.text: Subject to discovery: Usage exports contain stable account IDs and reporting periods.
An identity owner can support the pilot SSO integration.
CSMs retain approval of every customer-facing narrative.

questions.question: Who is the decision-maker for pilot funding, and when is the go/no-go review?
questions.why: Keeps the pilot tied to a named sponsor and a specific investment decision.

questions.question: Which source is authoritative when the export and CRM disagree?
questions.why: Prevents contradictory numerical claims and defines reconciliation rules.

questions.question: Who approves the narrative template and reviews the first 10 drafts?
questions.why: Makes accountability and acceptance criteria explicit.

questions.question: Which hosting region, retention period and model-processing terms are required?
questions.why: Data residency is a design constraint, not a post-build checkbox.

phases.name: Discover
phases.objective: Run a focused discovery workshop before committing the pilot build.
activities: Interview the sponsor and nominated pilot users.
Profile approved sample data and identify access gaps.
Agree baseline measures, acceptance thresholds and a go/no-go gate.
phases.exitCriteria: Sponsor signs off the pilot boundary, data access and evaluation plan.

phases.name: Design
phases.objective: Turn agreed outcomes and controls into a buildable pilot design.
activities: Map the bounded workflow and reviewer responsibilities.
Define interfaces, failure handling and evidence requirements.
Review the design with the operational and compliance owners.
phases.exitCriteria: Design and required control owners approve the implementation plan.

phases.name: Build
phases.objective: Build metric-grounded narratives, numerical checks, SSO and approval workflow.
activities: Implement only the agreed data inputs and workflow.
Add traceability, access controls and explicit failure states.
Evaluate representative and adversarial cases against the reference set.
phases.exitCriteria: The test cohort meets agreed quality thresholds; critical issues are resolved.

phases.name: Pilot
phases.objective: Evaluate usefulness and reliability with the agreed user cohort.
activities: Onboard pilot users and train reviewers.
Run a bounded trial against the baseline.
Capture errors, review effort and user feedback.
phases.exitCriteria: Sponsor reviews measured results and decides to stop, iterate or expand.

phases.name: Handover
phases.objective: Give the owner a controlled, maintainable next step.
activities: Document the workflow, limits and operational runbook.
Present the pilot findings and a separately scoped rollout option.
phases.exitCriteria: Named owner accepts the handover and the next-step decision is recorded.

drivers.detail: Confirm during discovery: One usage export and identity provider; no CRM write-back.
Metric definitions, periods and account matching need validation.
SSO configuration and role access for the pilot cohort.
Approved processing region and retention settings.
CSMs approve each narrative before customer use.

risks.risk: The model invents or misstates a number.
risks.mitigation: Agree a stop condition with the sponsor. Pass only verified metrics, validate numerical claims and block unsupported drafts.

risks.risk: Inconsistent reporting periods distort the story.
risks.mitigation: Freeze a metric dictionary and flag incomparable or missing periods.
Confirm deployment and processing terms before selecting a live model.

metrics.target: Proposed: agree a baseline in discovery, then test a 30% improvement.
Proposed: 100% of numerical claims reconcile to the supplied snapshot.
Proposed: 80% of drafts rated useful with minor edits.
